04 Anxiety and benzodiazepines · class card

Benzodiazepines

benzodiazepines · alprazolam · lorazepam · clonazepam · diazepam · chlordiazepoxide · oxazepam · temazepam · midazolam · triazolam

Key point
  • A benzodiazepine with an opioid or alcohol respiratory depression and hypotension; alone, breathing is usually only mildly slowed
  • Short half-life (alprazolam) rebound anxiety between doses and harsher withdrawal; a long-acting agent such as clonazepam lowers both
  • After daily use, never stop abruptly: withdrawal seizures; flumazenil in a long-term user can set them off too
  • Liver disease or old age: lorazepam, oxazepam or temazepam, cleared by glucuronidation alone
Drugs

Alprazolam Xanax: short-acting on the NBME Alprazolam labelThe Xanax label contraindicates strong CYP3A (cytochrome P450 3A) inhibitors such as ketoconazole and itraconazole, ritonavir excepted.

Lorazepam Ativan: glucuronidation only; intravenous or intramuscular Lorazepam labelThe Ativan label lists acute narrow-angle glaucoma as a contraindication.

Clonazepam Klonopin: the long-acting switch

Diazepam Valium, chlordiazepoxide, flurazepam: long-acting

Oxazepam, temazepam Restoril: glucuronidation only

Midazolam, triazolam: short-acting Half-life classesShort, under 6 hours: triazolam, midazolam. Intermediate, 6 to 50 hours: alprazolam, lorazepam, oxazepam, temazepam, clonazepam. Long, over 50 hours: diazepam, chlordiazepoxide, flurazepam. Tables differ: the NBME treats alprazolam as short-acting and clonazepam as the long-acting switch.

Clorazepate ⚠︎ pharm document line; no board source found yet

Mechanism

Binds its own site on the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) type A receptor chloride channel opens more often sedation, anxiolysis, seizure control Versus barbituratesBenzodiazepines raise how often the channel opens ("frenzodiazepines"). Barbiturates bind a different site, carry more risk of respiratory depression and coma, and are not reversed by flumazenil.

Long use GABA-A receptors downregulate tolerance withdrawal after an abrupt stop

Lorazepam, oxazepam, temazepam skip the oxidative liver step safer in liver disease and old age MnemonicLOT may help recall them: lorazepam, oxazepam, temazepam, safe in liver disease.

Uses

Anxiety, panic: a short-term bridge until a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) works

Insomnia: not first line (dependence)

Alcohol withdrawal: long-acting agents, or lorazepam with liver disease

Catatonia (first line)

Status epilepticus, procedural sedation, acute agitation

Adverse effects

Sedation, ataxia, anterograde amnesia; older adults: falls, confusion

Rebound anxiety between doses of a short-acting agent Interdose symptomsThe Xanax label reports early-morning anxiety and anxiety between doses in panic disorder on maintenance doses.

Physiologic dependence on prescribed use is not a use disorder

Addiction: higher with short-acting agents MnemonicATOM may help recall the more addictive group: alprazolam, triazolam, oxazepam, midazolam (alprazolam and oxazepam are intermediate in some tables).

Withdrawal after an abrupt stop; timing below

Disinhibition in an adolescent raises acute suicide risk

Respiratory depressionStupor, slow breathing, low blood pressure with an opioid or alcohol; alone, near-normal vital signs and pupils

Flumazenil is not routine: in a long-term user it can set off withdrawal and seizures

If breathing slows or blood pressure falls, choose airway, breathing and circulation support; naloxone if an opioid may be involved.

Withdrawal seizuresTremor, anxiety, then a seizure 1 to 2 days after a short-acting agent such as alprazolam is stopped

If a daily user must come off a benzodiazepine, choose a slow taper, ideally of a longer-acting agent.

Paradoxical agitationAn older adult or child turns confused and aggressive, typically within an hour of a dose

If agitation follows a benzodiazepine dose, choose tapering and stopping it; a higher dose only worsens it.

Practice
  1. 26-year-old woman seen 1 day after her second emergency visit this month sudden pounding heart, breathlessness and fear of dying, peaking within minutes examination, electrocardiogram and thyroid tests normal; alprazolam started follow-up in 2 weeks → Rebound anxiety → alprazolam's short half-life brings rebound anxiety and withdrawal symptoms, and a long-acting agent such as clonazepam lowers that risk; agranulocytosis belongs to clozapine and urinary retention to anticholinergic drugs
  2. 58-year-old man with cirrhosis admitted for a variceal bleed, now banded and stable severe anxiety and insomnia since admission; no alcohol for 3 months oriented; no tremor or sweating; no asterixis BP 118/72 mm Hg · HR 84/min → Lorazepam → lorazepam, like oxazepam and temazepam, undergoes only glucuronidation, which liver disease spares; long-acting chlordiazepoxide and diazepam are avoided when the liver is compromised
  3. 71-year-old man on long-term oxycodone for spinal stenosis trouble falling asleep for 3 weeks since his wife entered a nursing home drinks 2 glasses of wine nightly; lives alone RR 14/min · oxygen saturation 96% → Alprazolam → a benzodiazepine taken with an opioid or alcohol can bring respiratory depression and hypotension, and in older adults it adds confusion and falls; cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia comes first, and ramelteon is safe in older adults
  4. 39-year-old woman on clonazepam for panic disorder for 2 years, taken exactly as prescribed when a dose is late she feels shaky, sweaty and anxious no dose escalation, no early refills, no craving; working full time → Physiologic dependence → tolerance and withdrawal during supervised, prescribed use are expected physiology and do not count toward a use disorder, which needs problematic use with distress or impairment; a paradoxical reaction brings agitation and confusion, typically within an hour of a dose
  5. 52-year-old man has a generalized seizure on day 2 after elective knee replacement home medicine not continued on admission; taken nightly for a year for anxiety and sleep no alcohol; no seizure history tremulous, anxious · HR 114/min · glucose and sodium normal → Alprazolam withdrawal → a short-acting benzodiazepine stopped abruptly can bring withdrawal seizures within 1 to 2 days; bupropion causes seizures while it is taken, and stopping paroxetine brings discontinuation symptoms without seizures
